item.title: Java BufferedReader Versus Scanner: Which Stream Input Tool to Select
item.description:
“Java BufferedReader Versus Scanner: Which Stream Input Tool to Select”

When handling input streams in Java, developers often encounter a fundamental choice: employ the low-level efficiency of BufferedReader or opt for the higher-level parsing capabilities of Scanner. Deciding between these two utilities hinges entirely on the specific requirements of the task, particularly whether the goal is raw data reading or token-based interpretation.

What is the fundamental divergence in purpose between Java’s BufferedReader and Scanner when dealing with input streams?
